about: Physics blocks whose maths is a formula (ND3b): each keeps its id, ports and results, and its maths is the Equation below, with a name that says what happens.

params.description: thermal conductivity of the liquid alloy (Pozzo et al. 2012 give about 150; Konopkova et al. 2016 about 30; until MP21's iron rows)
thermal expansivity of the liquid alloy
specific heat of the liquid alloy

references: Labrosse, S. 2015, Physics of the Earth and Planetary Interiors 247, 36: thermal evolution of the core with a high thermal conductivity (the adiabatic heat flow q = k α g T / c_p). doi:10.1016/j.pepi.2015.02.002

Driscoll, P. and Bercovici, D. 2014, Physics of the Earth and Planetary Interiors 236, 36: on the thermal and magnetic histories of Earth and Venus (dynamo power from the CMB flux above the adiabat plus inner core buoyancy). doi:10.1016/j.pepi.2014.08.004
atoms.shown: q_conv = q − k α g T / c_p

equation.name: Heat the core sheds by churning
equation.formula: Fc = q - k * alpha * g * T / max(cp, tiny)

tiny.name: floor that keeps the division finite

alpha.name: how much it expands when hot

cp.name: specific heat of the liquid metal

Fc.name: heat carried by churning, beyond what conducts

source.text: Labrosse, S. 2015, Phys. Earth Planet. Inter. 247, 36

explain.curious: A hot core can lose heat and still make no field: if conduction alone can carry the heat away, the iron does not need to churn.
explain.science: Liquid iron conducts heat well, so part of what leaves the core's top is carried by conduction along the adiabat, q_ad = k α g T / c_p. Only the rest is carried by convection, and only convection stirs a dynamo. When the flux falls below q_ad the top of the core is stably layered.

params.description: fractional density contrast of what is let out (light elements at the inner core boundary, about 5%)
thermal expansivity of the liquid alloy
specific heat of the liquid alloy

references: Buffett, B. A., Huppert, H. E., Lister, J. R. and Woods, A. W. 1996, Journal of Geophysical Research 101, 7989: on the thermal evolution of the Earth's core (light elements released at the inner core boundary as a buoyancy source). doi:10.1029/95JB03539

Driscoll, P. and Bercovici, D. 2014, Physics of the Earth and Planetary Interiors 236, 36: on the thermal and magnetic histories of Earth and Venus (dynamo power from the CMB flux above the adiabat plus inner core buoyancy). doi:10.1016/j.pepi.2014.08.004
O'Rourke, J. G. and Stevenson, D. J. 2016, Nature 529, 387: powering Earth's dynamo with magnesium precipitation from the core. doi:10.1038/nature16495

equation.name: Dynamo power from light elements rising
equation.formula:
Fl = if mdot <= 0 then 0 else cp / max(alpha, tiny) * drho * mdot
Fd = Fc + Fl

mdot.name: light elements let out per square metre per second

tiny.name: floor that keeps the division finite

drho.name: density contrast of what is let out

alpha.name: how much it expands when hot

cp.name: specific heat of the liquid metal

Fd.name: power that drives the dynamo, as a heat flux

source.text: Buffett, B. A., Huppert, H. E., Lister, J. R. and Woods, A. W. 1996, J. Geophys. Res. 101, 7989
source.where: buoyancy at the inner core boundary

explain.curious: Earth's field may be older than its solid inner core. Once the inner core began to freeze, the light elements it pushed out rose like bubbles and gave the dynamo a second engine.
explain.science: A freezing inner core rejects light elements into the liquid above, and magnesium oxide can come out of solution at the core's top; either way buoyant fluid stirs the core. Its power is written as the heat flux that would give the same buoyancy, (c_p/α) Δρ/ρ ṁ/A, and added to the convected flux. A negative convected flux is a stable layer that the buoyancy must first overcome.
